summary:
[  edit  ]
The Transform XYZ  CHOP  is used to transform positions and vector. The difference between transforming a position vs. a vector is that a vector won't have the translation portion of the transformation applied to it.
The Transform XYZ  CHOP  first groups the channels from the first input by looking for ' x ', ' y ' and ' z ' as the last character in the channel names. Then it treats each of the sets created as either a Position or a Vector depending on the parameter choice. The second input can be connected, and must describe a transform in the same format of channels that the  Transform CHOP  supports. The second input is combined with the 'Transform' page parameters, and the resulting transform is applied to the input positions and vectors.
CHOPs with multiple-samples can be provided, which allows for larger amount of positional data to be transformed in a single  CHOP .
See also the  Transform CHOP .

inputs.description: Position/Vectors  - One or more sets of channels with 'x', 'y' and 'z' as the last character in their names, to be transformed.
Transform  - An optional additional transform that can be applied. Valid formats are the same as the  Transform CHOP .

parameters.label: Input 0 Type
parameters.name: input0type
parameters.description: ⊞  - Choose if the input 0 values should be treated as a position or a vectors. Vectors will not have the translation portion of the transform applied to them, and can be normalized before and/or after the transformation is applied.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Treat the input 0 values a positions.

parameters.label: Vector
parameters.name: vector
parameters.description: Treat the input 0 values a vectors.

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.name: innormalize
parameters.description: If the input is vectors, they can be normalized before the transformation is applied.

parameters.label: Custom Input Order
parameters.name: custinputorder
parameters.description: This allows the input order for input 1, if provided, to be ignored and overridden by a custom order chosen by the following two parameters.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.name: inxord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Changing the Transform order will change where things go much the same way as going a block and turning east gets you to a different place than turning east and then going a block. In matrix math terms, if we use the 'multiply vector on the right' (column vector) convention, a transform order of Scale, Rotate, Translate would be written as T * R * S * Position

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.name: inrord
parameters.description: ⊞  - As with transform order (above), changing the order in which the rotations take place will alter the final position and orientation. A Rotation order of Rx Ry Rz would create the final rotation matrix as follows R = Rz * Ry * Rx

parameters.label: Input 1 Pre Operation
parameters.name: input1preop
parameters.description: ⊞  - Operation(s) to apply on the transforms on Input 1, before they are combined with other transforms.

parameters.label: None
parameters.name: none
parameters.description: No operation is applied.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.name: invert
parameters.description: Invert the transform.

parameters.label: Transpose
parameters.name: transpose
parameters.description: Transpose the transform. This only has an effect for matrix format transforms.

parameters.label: Invert Transpose
parameters.name: inverttranspose
parameters.description: Invert and Transpose the transform. The transpose will only be done if the input is a matrix format transform.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.name: xord
parameters.description: ⊞  - See description from earlier Transform Order parameter.

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.name: rord
parameters.description: ⊞  - See description from earlier Rotate Order parameter.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.name: t
parameters.description: ⊞  - XYZ translation values.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.name: r
parameters.description: ⊞  - XYZ rotation, in degrees.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: s
parameters.description: ⊞  - XYZ scale to shrink or enlarge the transform.

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.name: p
parameters.description: ⊞  - XYZ pivot to apply the above operations around.

parameters.label: Pre Operation
parameters.name: preop
parameters.description: Turn this on to invert the transform generated by this page before combining it with the other terms.

parameters.label: Multiply Order
parameters.name: multiplyorder
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls how the input transform(s) are combined with the transform specified on this page. The below two descriptions use a multiply "vector on the right" convention (column vectors).

parameters.label: Input, then Transform Page
parameters.name: inputxformpage
parameters.description: The transforms will be combined as  Transform Page * Input .

parameters.label: Transform Page, then Input
parameters.name: xformpageinput
parameters.description: The transforms will be combined as  Input * Transform Page .

parameters.label: Un-matched Channels
parameters.name: unmatchedchans
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls how channels that don't match the naming convention for the various transform format are treated.

parameters.label: Warn
parameters.name: warn
parameters.description: Give a warning if transform channels that don't match any of the naming convenstions are found.

parameters.label: Ignore
parameters.name: ignore
parameters.description: Ignore (give no warning) if channels that don't match the naming convention are found.

parameters.label: Delete
parameters.name: delete
parameters.description: Delete all channels that don't match any of the naming conventions.

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.name: normalize
parameters.description: If the input data is being treated as vectors, they can be re-normalized after the transform by turning this on.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: Rename from
parameters.name: commonrenamefrom
parameters.description: The channel pattern to rename. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Rename to
parameters.name: commonrenameto
parameters.description: The replacement pattern for the names. The default parameters do not rename the channels. See  Pattern Replacement .

parameters.label: Channel Names:  c[1
parameters.description: 10:2] ambient

parameters.label: Rename To:  b[1
parameters.description: 5] amb    This example fetches channels  c1 c3 c5 c7 c9  and  ambient .

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.
